AARSNET_2025.notes: First annual report of AARSNET, the Assam state AMR surveillance network under NCDC (nodal centre Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, 12 government medical colleges): 14,179 priority-pathogen isolates from 13,369 unique patients in 2025 (the Discussion gives different totals: 14,346 reported, 11,834 and 13,299 after deduplication). Values are % resistant as printed. Genus-level organisms as printed. Pus aspirate (aspirated purulent material from a closed infected site; pus and wound swabs excluded) is mapped to deep; other sterile body fluids (CSF, pleural, peritoneal, synovial, pericardial) to sterile; IPD to ward. Location rows pool all specimens and carry no n (not printed with the charts); Table 4 location counts are recorded as counts. Several location figures do not reconcile with the specimen tables (S. aureus linezolid, Pseudomonas gentamicin, E. coli co-trimoxazole), see cell notes. Table 4 location counts do not sum to the Table 3 totals for Klebsiella (2,861 against 2,890), Pseudomonas (1,121 against 1,065) and S. aureus (1,684 against 1,711).
AARSNET_2025.reporting: Number tested, number resistant and % resistant by organism and specimen (blood, urine, pus aspirate, other sterile body fluids), all locations pooled; % resistant by location (OPD, IPD, ICU), all specimens pooled, as chart data labels without numbers tested. Isolate counts by specimen and by location.
AARSNET_2025.method: 12 government medical college laboratories in Assam; WHONET; NCDC AMR surveillance SOPs; CLSI; first isolate per patient, pathogen and specimen type in a hospital stay; pus aspirates from closed infected sites only (swabs excluded); vancomycin screen agar and broth microdilution; colistin broth microdilution in several laboratories.
AARSNET_2025.checking: Tables 3 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (automatic table extraction, specimen columns assigned from the header cells) and compared cell by cell with page images rendered at 2.6x; number resistant over number tested was also recomputed for every cell and all differences over 1 point are noted on the cell. Chart values (Figures 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22) are printed data labels from the text layer: each label was assigned to the bar whose end it sits next to on the same row, the series from the legend swatch colours, and the bar length measured against the axis ticks agreed with the label within 0.1 point for every bar; 0% labels of zero-length bars were placed by row position; every chart was also checked by eye on the rendered page. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which equal the printed page numbers in this report.

ASSAM.notes: Das et al. (J Pure Appl Microbiol 2023) studied all specimens hospital-wide at Assam Medical College and Hospital, Dibrugarh, an ICMR AMRSN site, October 2018 to March 2021: E. coli (2,237), Klebsiella spp. (2,673), Enterobacter spp. (177), Proteus spp. (125), Citrobacter (551), Acinetobacter (687), P. aeruginosa (646), S. aureus (1,786), E. faecium (617) and E. faecalis (200). The spp. groups appear as K. pneumoniae, E. cloacae and P. mirabilis. The tables print % resistant, so figures are 100 minus %R and intermediate counts as susceptible. Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin are for urinary isolates only; enterococcal gentamicin is high-level. Colistin (261 Gram-negative isolates tested by MIC, all susceptible) and VRE (1.2%, 10 of 817) were reported only in aggregate, so neither is shown per organism. MRSA was 44.7%; S. aureus vancomycin is 100% because no VRSA was found.
ASSAM.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Text extracted from the PDF text layer. Method: Figures come from Table 2 (Gram-negative) and Table 3 (Gram-positive), converted as 100 minus %R. Isolate numbers are the Table 2 column headers; the text on page 9 gives A. baumannii 550 and P. aeruginosa 590. Drugs not done for some organisms (cefepime, tobramycin except Pseudomonas, minocycline except Acinetobacter) were left out. S. aureus vancomycin 100% was entered from the text statement that no VRSA was detected, not from a table. Enterococcal gentamicin is high-level gentamicin (120 µg). Overall carbapenem resistance: Enterobacteriaceae 58.8%, non-fermenters 56.0%.

KIMS_KLEB.notes: Panigrahi et al. (Cureus 2025) studied Klebsiella pneumoniae from all clinical specimens (blood, urine, endotracheal tube samples, body fluids, sputum, pus, wounds and skin swabs) at Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar, October 2022 to September 2024; the authors excluded other Klebsiella species. Testing was by VITEK 2 with CLSI 2022 breakpoints. Figures are the overall % susceptible printed for all 7,942 isolates; intermediate results are not counted as susceptible (ciprofloxacin: 19.08% susceptible, 2.50% intermediate, 78.40% resistant). The paper also gives separate figures for ICU, non-ICU, community-acquired and hospital-acquired infections, which are not shown here.
KIMS_KLEB.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Text extracted from the PDF text layer. Method: Figures are the overall 'Total' sensitive percentages of Table 2 (page 10), as printed; they match the abstract (tigecycline 74.79%, gentamicin 39.45%, meropenem 34.34%, piperacillin-tazobactam 32.44%).
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: its own institution key (KIMS_BHUBANESWAR_KLEB, was KIMS_BHUBANESWAR): a different study from the same hospital is not an earlier edition of this one.

KIMS_STERILE.notes: Poddar et al. (Cureus 2026) studied sterile body fluids (CSF, pleural, ascitic and synovial) at Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar, January 2021 to December 2022: 2,307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive). It covers S. aureus (92), K. pneumoniae (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19) and Enterococcus (15). Susceptibility appears only as unlabelled bar charts and text, so all Gram-negative figures (accurate to about 1 to 2%) and the lower Gram-positive ones are approximate chart readings. The high staphylococcal figures (vancomycin, teicoplanin, linezolid, daptomycin, tigecycline) are stated for Staphylococcus spp. as a whole. S. aureus cloxacillin is 100 minus the 48.9% MRSA rate. K. pneumoniae ampicillin (41.9%) is implausible (intrinsic resistance), and P. aeruginosa amikacin reads below meropenem although the text ranks amikacin highest.
KIMS_STERILE.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Method: rendered the figure pages at 6x, calibrated the y-axis from detected tick-label centers (Fig 2: 0%=y1383, 100%=y368; Fig 1 baseline y1504), then extracted each bar's top and mid-bar color programmatically. Method: Values were measured off Figures 1 and 2 by calibrating the chart axis and matching bar colours to drugs; the colour-to-drug map was checked against figures quoted in the text (for example Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs the text's 41%, P. aeruginosa ceftazidime 20.9 vs 21%). Bars that could not be detected (P. aeruginosa ampicillin, amoxiclav and imipenem; Acinetobacter ampicillin, amoxiclav and ceftriaxone) were left out. The Staphylococcus spp. figures from the text were assigned to S. aureus because they match its bars. Pseudomonas spp. is shown as P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter spp. as A. baumannii. Enterococcal gentamicin is high-level gentamicin (86%, from the text). CoNS (n=43) and Streptococcus spp. (n=3) were not included. Gram-negative MDR, XDR and PDR rates: 21.6%, 14.2% and 3%.
issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems', i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).
Lead 2026-09-26: its own institution key (KIMS_BHUBANESWAR_STERILE, was KIMS_BHUBANESWAR): a different study from the same hospital is not an earlier edition of this one.

RIMS_IMPHAL_2025.notes: From the RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2026 (4th edition), section 4A 'RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2024-25' (book pages 23 to 48, PDF pages 38 to 63): 18,381 samples and 7,722 culture-positive isolates from July 2024 to June 2025. Specimen tables are for all locations; location tables (OPD, ward, ICU) are for all specimens, except the staphylococcal location table (Table 33), which is headed all specimens except urine (recorded as non-urine; some of its printed isolate numbers are all-specimen totals, see row notes), and the enterococcal location table (Table 45), which excludes faecal samples (recorded as all specimens). SS is recorded as sterile sites: the Table 7 note defines SS as fluid from sterile spaces (abdominal, intercostal tube, pancreatic drain, pericardial, peritoneal and pleural fluid) and Table 14 calls it sterile site samples, although the footnote to Table 6 expands SS as surgical site. The yearly trend tables print 0 for years in which an agent was not tested (in Table 24 cefoperazone-sulbactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, norfloxacin and tigecycline are 0 for 2020 to 2024 and have values only for 2025), so a 0 for these agents in the Enterobacterales tables (Tables 17 to 23), mainly in rows with few isolates, may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed, with a per-drug note. Two columns printed 0 throughout are left out as not tested (plazomicin in Table 20, fosfomycin for E. faecium in Table 45; see excluded). Imipenem is printed far below meropenem for E. coli and K. pneumoniae throughout. Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin. 'Staphylococcus spp.' in the organism tables (Tables 8, 9, 11, 12 and 15) is recorded as other coagulase-negative staphylococci: Table 25 lists the same 277 isolates as CoNS without species identification; the CoNS susceptibility rows (342) include the speciated CoNS. Table 36 prints different specimen totals (7,764 culture positive) from Table 6 (7,722), and 12 S. maltophilia where Table 35 lists 11.

RIMS_IMPHAL_2024.notes: RIMSH Antibiogram 2023-24 (the file name says 2023; the analysis period is 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024): 18,917 samples and 6,407 culture-positive isolates. Enterobacterales tables are by specimen for all locations; the A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa and enterococcal location tables cover all specimens except faeces (recorded as all specimens). There is no sterile-site antibiogram; the SS count column is recorded as sterile sites, as the 2026 policy defines SS (fluid from sterile spaces), although this report's text calls SS surgical sites. The report prints 0 for agents not tested in its trend tables, so a 0 in rows with few isolates may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed. Cefazolin is 0 for every organism in the blood table. 'Staphylococcus spp.' in the CoNS table is recorded as other (unspeciated) coagulase-negative staphylococci; the CoNS table prints one isolate fewer for each species than the distribution table (p14). The faeces table (p5) lists 183 diarrhoeagenic E. coli, while Tables 1.2 and 1.3 count 162 as diarrhoeagenic E. coli and 21 as E. coli, so Table 1.2's E. coli total (2,001) includes 21 faecal isolates. Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin.

RIMS_IMPHAL_2023.notes: Section 3 'RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2022-23' of the RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2024 (3rd edition; book pages 19 to 48, PDF pages 33 to 62), July 2022 to June 2023: 3,524 isolates studied (Table 1.1). The file was downloaded from the Wayback Machine copy (20240709) of the old rims.edu.in/secure URL and opens completely (164 pages). The report counts organisms in two ways: the organism table (Table 1.2) and the Enterobacteriaceae tables agree (E. coli 1,172, K. pneumoniae 545), but the non-fermenter, staphylococcal and enterococcal chapters use larger totals for the same period (A. baumannii 263 against 171, P. aeruginosa 314 against 234, S. aureus 554 against 470, E. faecalis 207 against 177, E. faecium 112 against 90); rows keep their own table's n and the organism counts are Table 1.2's, so these rows show count mismatches (source inconsistency). Some figures are not whole-number fractions of the printed n (for example A. baumannii ward 31.8% of 122), so for some agents fewer isolates were tested than the n shown. Colistin is printed 100 for every Enterobacteriaceae organism tested, including Serratia marcescens (intrinsically resistant). Specimen tables are for all locations; location tables are for all specimens (the enterococcal one except faeces). Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin. Where the report prints 0 for an agent in its trend tables it means not tested, so a 0 in rows with few isolates may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed.
RIMS_IMPHAL_2023.reporting: Percent susceptible with isolate numbers: Enterobacteriaceae for all specimens and by specimen (blood, urine, lower respiratory tract, superficial infection); P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii by specimen, A. baumannii by location; S. aureus (MSSA, MRSA) and CoNS from all specimens; E. faecalis and E. faecium by specimen and by location (OPD, ward, ICU).
RIMS_IMPHAL_2023.method: Identification and susceptibility testing per the ICMR SOP (conventional biochemical or automated system); data entered in the ICMR AMR surveillance portal, validated by the regional administrator and analysed with the iAMRSN portal.

ICMR_AMRSN_2024.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2024, part A: Enterobacterales (chapter 2) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 3), plus isolation counts from chapter 1. 99,027 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Colistin figures are percent intermediate. CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens) and Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations); the two sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17 (E. faecalis and E. faecium are counted separately). Part B of the ICMR AMRSN 2024 annual report (merged by the lead with Part A, chapters 1 to 3): typhoidal Salmonella, diarrhoeal pathogens, staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (invasive, Table 8.3) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"). Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) are left out. Fungal tables print S, I/SDD and R; only S is recorded. Several fungal percentages are printed 0.1 above the count ratio (e.g. 17/18 printed 94.5); recorded as printed. Isolates come from tertiary care hospitals; the report says the data do not reflect community AMR (p5). The ICMR network report for 2024 (21 regional centres; 99,027 culture-positive isolates). Extracted in two parts by table chapter and merged; the transcribed national summary used before this is superseded.
ICMR_AMRSN_2024.reporting: Percent susceptible with n/N tested. Enterobacterales: all specimens except urine and faeces, by species and by location (OPD, ward, ICU), and urine by species; non-fermenters: all samples except faeces by location, and by specimen (blood, LRT, SI, DI, CSF, urine). Colistin given as percent intermediate; yearly trends 2017 to 2024; cells with few isolates tested are printed as '-'.
ICMR_AMRSN_2024.method: Susceptibility testing per the ICMR Standard Operating Practices for Bacteriology and Mycology (PDF page 5); CLSI categories, breakpoint edition not stated. Data from tertiary-care network hospitals; the report says it does not reflect community AMR.

ICMR_AMRSN_2023.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2023, part A: organism counts (chapter 1 and chapter 2 section A), specimen-wise antibiograms by location for E. coli, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa (chapter 2 section B), Enterobacterales (chapter 3) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 4). 99,492 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Chapter 2 rows give blood, urine and pus/exudates by location (no all-location column); pus/exudates is one specimen type within the report's superficial infections, so these pus rows and counts are narrower than the chapter 4 pus (superficial infection) rows. Colistin figures are percent intermediate (chapters 3 and 4 footnotes; chapter 2 prints no footnote), and in chapter 2 several printed colistin percentages disagree with their own counts (recorded as printed, with conflicts). CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. The sample-wise non-fermenter tables (4.2, 4.5) print an n per specimen that matches the numbers tested, well below the isolate counts of Table 1.10. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens), Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations), and the top-5 lists of Tables 2.2 to 2.4 by specimen and location (blood, urine, pus/exudates); the sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17. ICMR AMRSN 2023, part B: typhoidal Salmonella (blood), diarrhoeal pathogens (stool), staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (national reference laboratory isolates) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"), plus the chapter 2 location tables for these organisms (S. Typhi blood, enterococci urine, S. aureus pus/exudates, faecal Salmonella and Aeromonas). 99,492 culture-positive isolates in the network in 2023. Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) or as counts without a percentage are left out. Several percentages are printed about 0.05 above the count ratio (e.g. 50/415 printed 12.1); recorded as printed. The yearly trend tables (2017 to 2023) are not recorded: the 2024 edition covers 2017 to 2024.
ICMR_AMRSN_2023.reporting: Percent susceptible with n/N tested. Specimen-wise antibiograms by location (OPD, ward, ICU) for blood, urine and pus/exudates (chapter 2); Enterobacterales from all specimens except urine and faeces, by species and by location, and from urine by species; carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets; non-fermenters from all samples by location and by specimen (blood, LRT, SI, DI, CSF, urine). Colistin given as percent intermediate in chapters 3 and 4; cells with few isolates tested are printed as '(-)'.
ICMR_AMRSN_2023.method: CLSI guidelines using disc diffusion or automated systems, colistin by broth microdilution (PDF page 76); breakpoint edition not stated. Data from tertiary-care network hospitals; the report says it does not reflect community AMR (PDF page 5).

ICMR_ESBL.notes: Gautam et al. (Indian J Med Res 2019) report an ICMR study of ESBL at four tertiary centres (AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry), October 2014 to March 2016: E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304) from blood, pus, sputum and body fluids, tested by Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion with CLSI breakpoints. Figures pool the resistant counts given separately for ESBL and non-ESBL isolates and show 100 minus %R, so intermediate counts as susceptible; colistin is the overall susceptibility printed in the text (E. coli 271 of 274, K. pneumoniae 229 of 234). For E. coli the pooled denominators reach 369, more than the 341 isolates collected. Some drugs were tested on far fewer isolates (E. coli ertapenem 90, cefpodoxime 68). ESBL was detected in 33% of E. coli (98 of 298) and 42% of K. pneumoniae (102 of 245).
ICMR_ESBL.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Overall figures were derived by pooling the Table III resistant counts (ESBL plus non-ESBL) per drug, for example E. coli amikacin 8/167 + 75/202 = 83/369 resistant, giving 77.5% susceptible. Table II gives % susceptible for each centre separately. ESBL was detected by the combined disc test. K. pneumoniae pooled denominators are at most 224, below the 304 isolates collected.
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: a multicentre research study, not a surveillance network report: kind "study", with a focus (two organisms, 2014 to 2016): shown, never pooled, not a profile.

NARSNET_2025.notes: Ninth NARS-Net annual report: 62 sentinel sites (medical college laboratories) in 34 states and UTs, priority bacterial pathogens January to December 2025 (first isolate per patient). All figures are percent resistant (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimens: pus aspirate (PA) is shown under deep infections (aspirates); other sterile body fluids (OSBF) as sterile body fluids, although NARS-Net OSBF also includes CSF and broncho-alveolar lavage. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows (outpatient, ward, ICU) come from bar charts with printed data labels; the report adds emergency department isolates to inpatient wards (shown here as wards). Cells marked x in the source (drug not in the panel for that specimen) are absent. Salmonella Typhi and Paratyphi A are reported separately; pefloxacin has no drug key. Candida from blood (997 isolates, fungal NRL) has no susceptibility table, so none is recorded (see excluded). The report warns that specimens come mostly from patients not responding to first-line antibiotics, which may skew resistance upward.
NARSNET_2025.reporting: Percent resistant (%R) with number tested and 95% CI, by pathogen and specimen type (blood, pus aspirate, other sterile body fluids, urine, stool), all location types combined; blood (and urine for E. coli and Enterococcus) also charted by location type (outpatient, inpatient, ICU) with printed data labels.
NARSNET_2025.method: WHONET 2024; CLSI M100 34th ed. (2024) interpretation; first isolate per patient, specimen type and pathogen (217,513 isolates, 202,573 unique patients); disk diffusion, broth microdilution, agar dilution or automated AST per the programme SOP; colistin by agar dilution or broth microdilution with EUCAST breakpoints; alert isolates (including colistin-resistant Gram-negatives) counted only after confirmation at the AMR-NRL, NCDC.
NARSNET_2025.checking: Tables 6 to 14 parsed from the PDF text layer (words grouped into rows by position) and every value then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 and cropped into halves. Figure 11 is an embedded image: labels read from the image zoomed 1.6 to 5 times, each against its bar. Trend Figures 16 (image) to 18: labels read on the rendered page and matched to their year by x position. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (1-based).

AIIMS_MEDWARDS.notes: Vaithiyam et al. (J Lab Physicians 2020) studied clinical isolates from all specimens in the medicine wards and ICU of AIIMS New Delhi; the years 2017 to 2019 are not confirmed in the paper's text. It covers A. baumannii (92 isolates), K. pneumoniae (86), E. coli (75), P. aeruginosa (22), E. faecium (15) and S. aureus (10). The tables print % resistant, so figures are 100 minus %R and intermediate counts as susceptible. The paper's text quotes some resistance figures as if they were susceptibility (cefoperazone-sulbactam 34.7%, imipenem 43%); the tables are used. Some drugs were tested on fewer isolates than the organism totals. Imipenem and meropenem disagree widely for E. coli (75.7% vs 19.5%) and K. pneumoniae (57% vs 16.3%). MRSA was 70% (7 of 10). Counts for P. aeruginosa, E. faecium and S. aureus are small.
AIIMS_MEDWARDS.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Text extracted from the PDF text layer (born-digital PDF, no OCR needed). Method: Figures come from Table 4 (Gram-negative) and Table 5 (Gram-positive), both headed as resistance patterns, converted as 100 minus %R. The resistance reading was confirmed by colistin (0% resistance, matching the text's 'no resistance') and by A. baumannii near 100% resistance to ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime and ceftazidime, consistent with the reported 89% P-XDR. Isolate numbers are from Table 2; the resistance tables have slightly different denominators because some drugs were not tested. JPNATC_ACINETO.notes: Kumari et al. (J Lab Physicians 2019) report five years of surveillance (2012 to 2016) of Acinetobacter from all clinical specimens at the JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS New Delhi: 3,744 isolates (28.9% of 16,210 isolates); 98.5% were A. baumannii, 1.4% A. lwoffii and 0.1% A. haemolyticus, all shown as A. baumannii. Tigecycline was not tested in 2012, so its figure covers 2013 to 2016. The table's yearly counts add up to about 4,680, more than the 3,744 isolates, so its percentages were used. Ampicillin-sulbactam, minocycline and cefoperazone-sulbactam were not tested.

DOON_CSOM.notes: Sammal et al. (Cureus 2024) studied ear discharge from patients with chronic suppurative otitis media at Government Doon Medical College, Dehradun, August 2022 to January 2024: 129 culture-positive isolates, tested by VITEK 2 with CLSI breakpoints. Only P. aeruginosa (46 isolates) and S. aureus (23) have full antibiograms. Figures are % susceptible as printed; intermediate results are not counted as susceptible. The S. aureus figures cover the 23 isolates of the paper's S. aureus table; the 18 MRSA isolates had a separate table and are not included, so MRSA made up about 43.9% of all S. aureus. Some drugs were tested on fewer isolates (for example piperacillin-tazobactam 38, imipenem 44). P. aeruginosa amikacin (57.8%) comes from the paper's discussion, not its table, and the cefoperazone figure is cefoperazone-sulbactam.

GMC_SRINAGAR_2024_H1.notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (January to June 2024) of the Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar. IPD (inpatient wards) is recorded as ward; ICU is separate. The overall tables are recorded as all specimens, all settings; the ICU tracheal aspirate tables as respiratory, ICU. The overall Gram-negative table prints genus-level rows (Acinetobacter sp. n=30, Klebsiella sp. n=56, Pseudomonas sp. n=44) beside the species rows, and the blood table a Pseudomonas spp. row beside P. aeruginosa; the app has one key per genus, so only the species rows are recorded (see excluded). Many location and tracheal aspirate cells print a value where the overall table prints "-" (not tested) for the same organism and drug (e.g. E. coli ampicillin-sulbactam, Klebsiella tobramycin); these are marked as conflicts. Counts: the inpatients, OPD and ICU columns of the overall tables are recorded as all specimens by location (species rows only); for every organism they sum to fewer than the table's printed number of isolates (e.g. E. coli 548 of 575), and their ICU figures are smaller than the ICU isolates of the tracheal aspirate table alone for A. baumannii (42 against 52, or 76 with the 24 blood ICU isolates), K. pneumoniae (13 against 41) and E. coli (17 against 18), and smaller than the blood, urine and tracheal aspirate ICU rows together for P. aeruginosa (35 against 20, 1 and 26) and S. aureus (9 against 7 and 6); B. cepacia has 25 ICU isolates in the overall table but 28 in the blood ICU row. So the location columns do not agree with the specimen tables. Zero-isolate strata of the blood and urine tables are recorded as 0 counts. Many blood, urine and tracheal aspirate strata have fewer than 30 isolates, and several printed percentages are not possible for the printed n (marked with a caution). Vancomycin was not tested for S. aureus. P. aeruginosa overall cefepime (100%) contradicts the blood and urine tables and is marked as a conflict.
GMC_SRINAGAR_2024_H1.reporting: Percent susceptible. Overall Gram-negative and Gram-positive tables (all specimens and locations) with the number of isolates and a split by location (inpatients, OPD, ICU); blood and urine tables by location (IPD, OPD, ICU) with n per location; ICU tracheal aspirate tables (Gram-negative and S. aureus) with n.
GMC_SRINAGAR_2024_H1.method: CLSI M100, 34th edition (2024). The report states that organisms with fewer than 30 isolates were excluded (applied to the overall tables); vancomycin for S. aureus was not tested (no MIC method available).
GMC_SRINAGAR_2024_H1.checking: All tables parsed from the PDF text layer (words rebuilt from character positions, because the scaled glyphs defeat word extraction, and assigned to columns by the table ruling lines or header positions); every value, n and location label then compared by eye with the rendered pages (scale 2.5 whole pages; pages 2, 4 and 6 again at scale 3.2 in two halves each), 2026-09-26.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 386 cells (seeded sample 96), all 46 row n, organisms and settings, and all 34 counts re-read against the page images (whole pages at scale 2.5, table crops at scale 3 to 4) before comparing with the file; 0 transcription errors and no IPD/OPD/ICU swaps (page 7 prints vancomycin before linezolid, page 5 after it; both mapped correctly; the blood IPD K. pneumoniae and tracheal aspirate K. pneumoniae ceftazidime cells are blank on the page and correctly left out).

The 19 conflicts are confirmed as printed: 18 cells where the overall table (page 2) prints "-" (not tested) but a location or tracheal aspirate table prints a value (E. coli ampicillin-sulbactam 0 in blood IPD and ICU, urine IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates; K. pneumoniae ampicillin-sulbactam 0 in blood IPD, urine IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates, and tobramycin 18.8, 33.3 and 33.3 in urine IPD, OPD and ICU; A. baumannii ceftriaxone 0 in blood IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates, and Acinetobacter spp. urine IPD; E. coli urine IPD aztreonam 100 and tobramycin 66.7), and overall P. aeruginosa cefepime 100 against 24% and 30% (blood IPD and ICU) and 71.4% (urine OPD). The only other such cell, urine IPD K. pneumoniae ampicillin 0 (overall IR), is already marked intrinsic.

Cautions for percentages no whole number of isolates gives are confirmed as printed: blood ICU A. baumannii imipenem 24.3 (n=24), urine ICU K. pneumoniae piperacillin-tazobactam 50 (n=1), tracheal aspirate E. coli (5 figures, n=18) and P. aeruginosa (3 figures, n=26); blood ICU E. coli imipenem 50 and meropenem 100 (n=4) are as printed.

ICU counts: the row and file notes are correct that the overall table's ICU column is smaller than the tracheal aspirate ICU isolates for A. baumannii (42 against 52), K. pneumoniae (13 against 41) and E. coli (17 against 18), but only the A. baumannii tracheal aspirate row had a note. The ICU column is also smaller than the blood, urine and tracheal aspirate ICU rows together for P. aeruginosa (35 against 47) and S. aureus (9 against 13), and than the blood ICU row alone for B. cepacia (25 against 28). Added these to notes and a note to each of those rows. The overall table's location columns sum to less than its printed n for every organism, as the row notes say.

Against the full-year 2024 report (GMC_SRINAGAR_2024): several full-year figures are impossible if this report's isolates are part of the full-year strata (e.g. blood Burkholderia, urine ICU E. coli carbapenems, blood ICU Pseudomonas); these are marked in that file. Blood OPD A. baumannii has 2 isolates here but the full-year blood table has none.
Lead 2026-09-26: the full-year 2024 report contradicts some of these figures (listed as conflicts in GMC_SRINAGAR_2024); these half-year figures are kept as printed.

GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H1.notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (January to June 2023) of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar (cover letter dated 4 October 2023), with sections for pus, blood and urine; no location split, so every row is all settings. The pus lists and the blood tables print no isolate numbers, so those rows have no n; the organism counts of pages 2 (pus) and 6 (blood) are recorded as counts. The urine Gram-positive table prints only shares (Enterococcus 78.4% and S. aureus 21.5% of 293 Gram-positive growths; MRSA 49.2%, MSSA 50.7% of S. aureus), so its rows have no n. Blood shares printed: MRSA 55.17% and MSSA 44.8% of S. aureus (174), MR-CoNS 52% and MS-CoNS 48% of CoNS (201). The pus lists and blood Gram-negative table include "Ceftazidime-tazobactam" / "Ceftazidime+ Tazobactum", which has no drug key and is not recorded. The E. coli and Klebsiella pus lists of the July to December 2023 report repeat several of these figures exactly.
GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H1.reporting: Percent susceptible, all locations together. Pus: one list of percentages per organism (organism counts on page 2, no n in the lists). Blood: Gram-positive (MRSA, MSSA, MR-CoNS, MS-CoNS, Enterococcus) and Gram-negative tables without isolate numbers (organism counts on page 6). Urine: Gram-negative table with the number of isolates; Gram-positive table with each organism's share of isolates only.
GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H1.method: Not stated. The report notes that vancomycin MIC testing (recommended by CLSI for staphylococci) is not done in the laboratory.

Two separate readings of every table: pass 1 from whole pages rendered at scale 2.5, pass 2 from crops at scale 3 to 4 (wide tables in halves, column headers from rotated crops, a contrast-enhanced crop for the blurred row labels of page 7). The two readings were compared automatically: 365 of 365 values and counts agreed. In the blood Gram-negative table (page 8) the unruled Burkholderia row, which has blank cells, was assigned to columns by measuring each value's position against the column positions of the complete E. coli row (grid overlay and ink-segment positions on the deskewed rows). No cell was unreadable except the Enterococcus share of isolates on page 7 (not needed).

GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H2.notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (July to December 2023) of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar, with sections for blood, urine, and pus and body fluids; no location split, so every row is all settings. The blood tables print each organism's share of isolates (e.g. E. coli 7.8% of 255 Gram-negative isolates) but no isolate numbers, and the pus lists print none, so those rows have no n; the organism counts of pages 1 (blood), 4 (urine) and 7 (pus) are recorded as counts. MRSA were 42% and MSSA 58% of blood S. aureus, MR-CoNS 63% and MS-CoNS 37% of blood CoNS. Urine MRSA (4 isolates) and MSSA (6) percentages such as 65% and 93% cannot be produced by 4 or 6 isolates (source error, recorded as printed). Several pus figures repeat the January to June 2023 report exactly (e.g. E. coli tigecycline 97, amikacin 75, cefoperazone-sulbactam 68, piperacillin-tazobactam 58, ceftriaxone 22, ampicillin-sulbactam 7; MRSA tetracycline 86, erythromycin 27; Enterococcus vancomycin 88, high-level gentamicin 55), while others differ. Pus lists include "Ceftazidime-tazobactam" and the urine table "Ceftazidime + Clavulanic acid", which have no drug key and are not recorded. Candida susceptibility was not done (no reagents).
GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H2.reporting: Percent susceptible, all locations together. Blood: Gram-positive (MRSA, MSSA, MR-CoNS, MS-CoNS, Enterococcus) and Gram-negative tables giving each organism's share of isolates but no isolate numbers (organism counts on page 1). Urine: Gram-negative and Gram-positive tables with the number of isolates. Pus and body fluids: one list of percentages per organism (organism counts on page 7, no n in the lists).
GMC_SRINAGAR_2023_H2.method: Not stated. The report says vancomycin was not tested for staphylococci (MIC method required), colistin and polymyxins are not reported (MIC only), "-" means intrinsically resistant or not tested, and patterns for fewer than 30 isolates are not given (CLSI), although blood E. coli (20 isolates) and Klebsiella (16) are shown.

GMC_SRINAGAR_2021.notes: Antibiogram of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar, for July 2020 to July 2021 (cover letter dated 25 November 2021; the pus and body fluid section covers July 2020 to June 2021). Blood: the organism counts are printed separately for the NICU and for "IPD and ICU"; both are recorded as inpatient counts (NICU patients are inpatients), which the app adds up. The Gram-negative table's isolate numbers equal NICU plus IPD and ICU for E. coli (30), Klebsiella (89), Pseudomonas (39) and Acinetobacter (158), so it covers all blood cultures (IPD, ICU and NICU) and is recorded as all inpatients; Burkholderia is printed as 37 there but 32 in the counts. The Candida antifungal table (110 isolates, 39.4%) matches the NICU count (Candida 110) and the NICU chart (279 positive specimens; 110/279 = 39.4%), and the IPD and ICU counts list no Candida, so it is recorded as ICU (NICU). C. albicans 32 (29%), non-albicans 78 (71%); the report attributes the flucytosine resistance to C. krusei. The blood table's "Quinolones" column (a drug class) and the "Ceftazidime/tazobactam" and "Ticarcillin" entries of the pus lists have no drug key and are not recorded. Urine rows have no n (only each organism's share of isolates: E. coli 70%, Klebsiella 12%, Enterococcus 8%, P. aeruginosa 6%, S. aureus 2% with MRSA 30% and MSSA 70%, Acinetobacter 1%, Proteus 1%). Several pus Enterococcus percentages (11 isolates: vancomycin 93, ampicillin 48, penicillin 47) cannot be produced by 11 or fewer isolates (source error, recorded as printed).
GMC_SRINAGAR_2021.reporting: Percent susceptible. Blood: organism counts for NICU and for IPD and ICU, one Gram-negative table with the number of isolates (IPD, ICU and NICU together) and a Candida antifungal table. Pus and body fluids: one list of percentages per organism with its isolate number. Urine: one list of percentages per organism with its share of isolates only.

Two separate readings of every table: pass 1 from whole pages rendered at scale 2.5, pass 2 from crops at scale 2.6 to 3 (landscape pages in halves). The two readings were compared automatically: 256 of 256 values, isolate numbers and counts agreed; page 6 is a second scan of page 5 with the same values. No cell was unreadable.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 184 cells (including the seeded 40% sample of 74), all 23 row n values and all 21 counts were read blind from the page images (scale 3 to 4.5, landscape pages in parts) and compared with the file automatically: 0 differences, nothing corrected; page 6 re-read as a second scan of page 5 with the same values.

Blood Gram-negative table recorded as inpatient: supported. Its n equal the NICU plus the IPD and ICU counts of page 3 (E. coli 8 + 22 = 30, Klebsiella 19 + 70 = 89, Pseudomonas 0 + 39 = 39, Acinetobacter 34 + 124 = 158), and the whole-blood block of page 3 (3520 samples) is exactly IPD and ICU (3060) plus NICU (460), with no OPD block.

Candida antifungal row recorded as icu (NICU): supported. Its 110 isolates (39.4%) equal the NICU Candida count (110) and 110 of the 279 NICU positive specimens of the page 4 chart, and the IPD and ICU block lists no Candida.

Burkholderia count mismatch confirmed as printed: 37 isolates in the Gram-negative table (page 5 and its second scan, page 6) against 32 in the IPD and ICU counts (page 3) and the IPD chart (page 4), none in the NICU (a source inconsistency, already in the row note).

Cells not kept, re-read on page 9: pus Enterococcus (n=11) vancomycin 93, ampicillin 48, penicillin 47 (cautions) and gentamicin 52 (printed as plain "Gentamycin", intrinsic) are printed that way (source, not transcription). Pus, urine settings "all" (no location split) and specimens confirmed.

GMCH_CHANDIGARH_2018.notes: Antibiotic Prescription Guidebook of the GMCH-32 Antibiotic Stewardship Program (44 pages; PDF pages 10 to 32 hold the protocol boxes). The document says the recommendations are based on isolates of the last 6 months without naming the months, so no end month is given. For each pathogen only the three to four most susceptible agents are printed (as the guidebook states on p8), so drugs that are missing were not necessarily tested and the printed set favours active agents. Syndromes are recorded as specimens: BSI as blood, UTI and complicated UTI as urine, SSTI as pus, pneumonia as respiratory; ICU as ICU, WARDS as wards, OPD as OPD. Every organism number except S. Typhi (20) is a multiple of 6, and several percentage sets are exact fractions of one sixth of the printed number (for example ICU BSI Acinetobacter n=42 with 71, 57, 43 and 29%, which are 5, 4, 3 and 2 of 7; ICU BSI S. aureus n=30 with 100, 80, 60 and 40%, fifths), which suggests the printed isolate numbers may have been scaled up from a shorter period; they are recorded as printed but may overstate the isolates tested. Counts are the organism numbers of each box (they sum to the printed totals). Enterococcal gentamicin is printed without 'high level'. The OPD SSTI box (p32) carries a 'WARDS MICROBIOLOGY DATA' header, taken as a template error. Data are from 2018; the app keeps them out of pooled views. Page numbers are PDF pages (printed page number plus 4). The printed 'Total no. of isolates' is not used as the isolate number: every value except S. Typhi (20) is a multiple of 6, most percentage sets fit one sixth of it, and the department charts (pp35 to 37) print exactly half of each box number, so the number tested is unknown (second reader's fit analysis): rows are kept without an isolate number, so they are shown but never pooled or used by reasoning.
GMCH_CHANDIGARH_2018.reporting: Syndrome by location boxes (ICU: BSI, UTI, SSTI, pneumonia; wards: BSI, complicated UTI, SSTI; OPD: BSI, complicated UTI, SSTI), each with the total isolates, the most common pathogens with their number and share, and for each pathogen three to four (sometimes more) agents with percent susceptible; agents with the same percentage are printed together as 'Drug(=Drug2=Drug3) (x%)'.
GMCH_CHANDIGARH_2018.method: Disc diffusion, CLSI 2018 (printed on p8: 'based on Disc diffusion method of CLSI-2018 ... not on MIC values').
GMCH_CHANDIGARH_2018.checking: Pages are printed rotated 90 degrees; the text was extracted with a second PDF library (another parser reverses it) and every box was read on the rotated page images at scale 3.5. Each transcribed box text was compared with the text layer (48 of 49 match character for character; the p30 Enterococcus box differs only because the text layer interleaves the organism label, and was checked on the image). Organism numbers sum to each box's printed total in all 10 boxes.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 228 cells, all 49 row n values and all 49 counts re-read against the rotated page images (scale 3.5), each value read before comparing; 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. The 7 intrinsic cells (enterococcal 'Gentamicin' 17, 50, 42, 50, 50 and 100%, and OPD urine Enterococcus cefotaxime 100%) are printed as recorded.

Isolate numbers: every printed percentage can come from its row n except OPD urine Klebsiella cefepime 87% (n=36; 31 of 36 is 86.1%). With n/6, 39 of 48 rows fit (S. Typhi, n=20, not divisible), and in several rows n/6 is the smallest number of isolates that gives all printed values (ICU pneumonia Pseudomonas, n=408: 62, 56, 53 and 43% need at least 68 = 408/6). Rows that do not fit n/6: ICU BSI Enterococcus, ICU SSTI Pseudomonas and E. coli, ward BSI S. aureus, Enterococcus, Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, OPD urine E. coli and Klebsiella.

The source prints a second, different count for the same strata: the department-wise distribution charts (pp35 to 37) give exactly half of each box's organism numbers in their ICU columns (blood 21, 15, 12, 12, 3, 3 against 42, 30, 24, 24, 6, 6; urine and pus likewise) and, summed over departments, for ward blood and for ward plus OPD urine; every label on those charts is a multiple of 3. The only wording about n is 'Total no. of isolates' in each box and 'organisms isolated in the Microbiology laboratory over last 6 months' (p6); nothing says whether isolates, tests or samples were counted. n left as printed.
Lead 2026-09-26: n set to unknown on 49 rows and 49 counts moved to excluded, on the second reader's evidence that the printed isolate numbers are not the numbers tested.

HAYES_URO.notes: Bhargava et al. (Front Microbiol 2022) studied clean-catch midstream urine isolates at Hayes Memorial Mission Hospital, Prayagraj, November 2018 to December 2019. It covers E. coli (183 isolates), Proteus (23, not speciated), K. pneumoniae (22), Citrobacter (21), P. aeruginosa (21), S. aureus (20), Enterococcus (18, not speciated) and E. cloacae (17). Figures are % susceptible as printed. Of all isolates, 96.0% were multidrug-resistant; 40.4% of E. coli and none of the K. pneumoniae produced ESBL. The enterococcal gentamicin figure is high-concentration gentamicin. Imipenem runs well above meropenem for E. coli (57.4% vs 37.2%), K. pneumoniae (72.7% vs 40.9%) and P. aeruginosa (90.5% vs 23.8%), so read carbapenem figures with care. Apart from E. coli, each organism has 23 isolates or fewer.
HAYES_URO.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Data from Table 4 (page 6), text-extracted (machine-readable PDF, not scanned). Method: Figures come from Table 4 (page 6), confirmed as susceptibility by the text (for example amikacin 'effective against 77.0% of E. coli'); isolate numbers are the column headers; not-tested results were left out. Ceftazidime-clavulanate (an ESBL confirmation disc) and novobiocin (an identification test) are not shown as treatments. S. epidermidis (n=8) was not included. The S. aureus clindamycin figure (55.0%) is ambiguous in the source row (55.0% and 62.5% across the Gram-positive columns) and was assigned to S. aureus, with 62.5% to S. epidermidis.

Accepted as correct because clindamycin is clinically tested against staphylococci (not enterococci, which are intrinsically resistant), making S. aureus 55.0% / S. epidermidis 62.5% the consistent reading; the extraction correctly omits

LHMC_2024.notes: Antimicrobial data chapter of the LHMC Antibiotic Policy 2025 for January to December 2024 (Lady Hardinge Medical College and associated hospitals). The susceptibility tables print no n, so every row has n null; isolate counts by organism and specimen (all locations) are recorded from Tables 2 and 4. Totals over all organisms: urine 1971, blood 928, pus 1563, other sterile body fluids 341, LRI samples 529; inpatients 2582, outpatients 1678, ICU 646. The "PUS + OSBF" tables combine pus and other sterile body fluids and are mapped to pus (the pus and OSBF counts are recorded separately); LRT/LRI tables are mapped to respiratory; IPD is mapped to wards. Organisms are reported at genus level (Klebsiella spp., Acinetobacter spp., Pseudomonas spp., Enterococcus spp.); Salmonella Typhi and Paratyphi are reported together. Each organism and specimen has an all-locations table and a by-location table; both are kept (different settings).
LHMC_2024.reporting: Percent susceptible by organism for urine, blood, pus with other sterile body fluids (OSBF) and lower respiratory tract samples, for all locations together and by location (IPD, OPD, ICU); numbers of isolates by organism and specimen. No numbers of isolates or numbers tested are printed with the susceptibility tables.
LHMC_2024.checking: Every susceptibility table (Tables 6, 8 to 25, PDF pp 20 to 33) and the isolate tables (Tables 2 and 4, pp 18 to 19) read from the PDF text layer, one line per drug, and compared value by value with the rendered page images; cells missing from a text line (blank in the table) were placed by column on the image (2026-09-26). Page numbers are PDF pages; the printed page numbers are 12 lower.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every susceptibility table (Tables 6 and 8 to 25, PDF pp 20 to 33, including the continuations of Tables 12, 14 and 16 on pp 26 to 28) re-read by eye from page renders (scale 2.6 to 3, one crop per table or table half) and written down before comparing with the file: all 682 cells (the seeded 30% sample of 205 cells is part of this), the organism, specimen and location of all 50 rows, and all 42 counts (Tables 2 and 4, pp 18 and 19). 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected, so no table needed a re-read under the 2% rule.

Second reader: location checked on every row against the printed column headers (IPD, OPD, ICU; Table 13 prints only IPD and ICU columns, hence its two rows): no column swap anywhere. IPD as ward fits Table 3, which counts inpatients (2582), outpatients (1678) and ICU (646) as separate groups.

Second reader: no isolate number is printed for any susceptibility table or row (every heading and column header of Tables 6 to 25 re-read, and the text layer of pp 17 to 33 searched); the only isolate numbers are in the isolation Tables 1 to 4, so n null is right on all 50 rows.

Second reader: specimen headings confirmed as printed: Tables 16 to 21 say "PUS + OSBF" (pus with other sterile body fluids, mapped to pus; by Table 4, OSBF is 78 of 440 E. coli, 54 of 239 Klebsiella spp., 82 of 230 Acinetobacter spp. and 26 of 556 S. aureus isolates in that pool); Table 22 says "LRT Sample" and Tables 23 to 25 say "LRI" (Table 1 "LRI SAMPLES", Table 4 "LRT SAMPLE", text "Lower Respiratory Tract Samples"), mapped to respiratory.

Second reader: the 11 intrinsic cells (Acinetobacter spp. ampicillin: blood 24 all, 32 IPD, 0 ICU; pus + OSBF 19 all, 21 IPD, 27 OPD, 0 ICU; LRT 3 all, 3 IPD, 25 OPD, 2 ICU) are printed that way, not misreadings. No count-table mismatch: each organism's five specimen counts in Table 4 add up to its Table 2 total. Blank cells (no dash printed) in Table 10 (Salmonella cefuroxime) and Table 22 (Klebsiella spp. ceftazidime and tetracycline, Pseudomonas spp. ampicillin-sulbactam) are rightly left out.

Second reader: printed as recorded but worth a look: Table 10 gives E. coli blood tetracycline 98% against doxycycline 54% (tetracycline-susceptible isolates count as doxycycline-susceptible, so one of the two is likely a source error); no validator rule flags it, and it is left as printed.

Lead 2026-09-26 (review round 2): urine E. coli ceftriaxone 30% and cefotaxime 29% carry a conflict: the text on page 20 gives about 30% ESBL producers for the same isolates (Klebsiella, ESBL 50% and ceftriaxone 49%, is consistent).

MGJAIPUR_BSI.notes: Purohit et al. (J Lab Physicians 2024) studied blood culture isolates from patients with bloodstream infection at Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Hospital, Jaipur, October 2022 to September 2023: K. pneumoniae (309), E. coli (191), Acinetobacter (138), Enterococcus (125), P. aeruginosa (50) and S. aureus (46). Figures are % susceptible as printed. Klebsiella, Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas were reported as spp. and are shown under their main species; Enterococcus was not split, though the text gives 85% E. faecium and 12.8% E. faecalis. Colistin is 100% for every Gram-negative organism, printed under a column header marked as intermediate. Drugs not tested or intrinsically resistant were left out, not shown as 0. Enterococcal gentamicin is high-level. CRE was 50.2% (269 of 536), MRSA 56.5% (26 of 46) and VRE 7.2% (9 of 125).
MGJAIPUR_BSI.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Text extracted from JLP 2024;16(4):501-506, Purohit et al, MGMC&H Jaipur BSI study. Method: Figures come from Table 1 (Gram-positive) and Table 2 (Gram-negative), both headed as susceptibility; the direction was confirmed by the text (vancomycin, linezolid and daptomycin 100% in S. aureus; oxacillin 43.5% matching 56.5% MRSA).

RML_ICU.notes: A 2024 Cureus study of ICU blood cultures at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow, June 2022 to June 2023: 213 of 669 samples (31.8%) grew. Testing was by VITEK 2 with CLSI M100 2022 breakpoints. It covers K. pneumoniae (41), Acinetobacter (38, shown as A. baumannii), S. aureus (20), P. aeruginosa (19) and Enterococcus (9, not speciated), all small numbers. Figures are % susceptible as printed on the paper's bar charts. MRSA was 77.6%; metallo-beta-lactamase producers were 64.3% of Gram-negative isolates (Acinetobacter 71%, P. aeruginosa 68.4%, K. pneumoniae 65.9%) and ESBL producers 19.6% (K. pneumoniae 26.8%). The enterococcal gentamicin figure matches the text's 77.8% high-level gentamicin resistance. Coagulase-negative staphylococci (46 isolates), the commonest isolate, are not included.
RML_ICU.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Susceptibility data is in bar-chart figures (Figure 1 gram-positive, Figure 2 gram-negative), NOT text tables; extracted the printed data-labels from the embedded chart images. Method: Figures are the data labels printed on Figure 1 (Gram-positive) and Figure 2 (Gram-negative); there are no susceptibility tables. The Enterococcus clindamycin bar had no printed value and was left out. Methicillin-resistant CoNS 66%; metallo-beta-lactamase producers among E. coli 60%.

RMLIMS_LUCKNOW_2022.notes: Dr. RMLIMS Lucknow Microbiology Newsletter, Issue 10 (February 2023), annual antibiograms for January to December 2022. Each specimen page has organism tables whose rows are OPD, IPD (recorded as wards) and ICU strata identified only by the colour of the Number cell; the report prints rows only for organisms or groups it could report. To reach 30 isolates the report groups organisms: "Lactose fermenters" (E. coli, Citrobacter, Klebsiella and Enterobacter spp.) rows are not recorded because no organism key fits a mixed Enterobacterales group (see excluded). "Other Staphylococcus spp." is defined by the report as coagulase-negative staphylococci and is recorded as CoNS. "Pseudomonas spp." rows are recorded under the P. aeruginosa key, as printed. Specimens: "Body fluids" are sterile body fluids including CSF (recorded as sterile body fluids); "Respiratory specimen" includes sputum, BAL, throat swab, nasal swab, bronchial aspirate and endotracheal aspirate; "Pus" includes pus, pus swab, catheter tip, CVP line, shunt, tissue, bone marrow, genital and ear samples, stool and urethral swab (recorded as pus). Codes follow the report's abbreviation list (AB amphotericin B, MYC micafungin, CAS caspofungin, VRC voriconazole); NX, not in that list, is the norfloxacin column the urine pages annotate. Cells printed "-", "**" or blank are left out. Many rows have fewer than 30 isolates (the report's own rule is 30). The live URL returns 404; the PDF was downloaded from the Internet Archive capture of the same URL (2024-03-30).
RMLIMS_LUCKNOW_2022.reporting: Percent susceptible (colour-coded >90%, 70 to 90%, <70%) with the number of isolates, by specimen (blood, sterile body fluids including CSF, respiratory, pus and other samples, urine) and organism or organism group; each row is one location (OPD, IPD or ICU), shown only by the colour of its Number cell. Candida: percent susceptible by specimen for isolates tested on request, not split by location.
RMLIMS_LUCKNOW_2022.method: AST method and breakpoint edition not stated for the antibiograms. The report's colistin and vancomycin MIC tables are from VITEK 2 COMPACT (bioMerieux) and cite CLSI M100 31st edition (2022) for colistin categories.
RMLIMS_LUCKNOW_2022.checking: Antibacterial tables (PDF pages 8 to 14): cell text parsed from the PDF text layer automatically (ruled table cells; rotated drug headers rebuilt from character positions), and the location of each row taken from the background colour of its Number cell sampled on the page rendered at scale 3 (OPD pink, IPD blue, ICU yellow, as in each page legend). Every value, every n and every row location was then compared by eye with the rendered pages, with the parsed text overlaid on each table image (scale 3): no differences. The values are percentages: they agree with the printed colour code (for example 77 on an amber 70 to 90% cell where n is 259) and several exceed the row n. The row n values also agree with the legible bars of the organism charts on the same pages (for example respiratory IPD Klebsiella 61, Pseudomonas 53, Acinetobacter 47; urine ICU Enterococcus 34, E. coli 30, Pseudomonas 30), which confirms the colour-based location of those rows. Antifungal table (page 18): parsed from the text layer and compared with the page image the same way. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (the printed page number is one lower on the antibiogram pages).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 434 cells (the seeded sample of 108 included), all 42 row n values and all 42 row locations re-read against the page images (PDF pages 8 to 14 and 18, rendered at scale 3 to 4); 0 errors, nothing corrected; every table was read in full.

Row locations: the fill colour of every Number cell, taken from the PDF vector fills, was compared with each page legend (OPD pink, IPD blue, ICU yellow): all 42 agree with the recorded setting. To reach 30 isolates the report groups organisms: "Lactose fermenters" (E. coli, Citrobacter, Klebsiella, Proteus and Providencia spp.), "Non lactose fermenters" (Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter spp.) and "Staphylococcus spps" (S. aureus and CoNS); these rows have no organism key and are not recorded, so this edition contributes only urine rows (E. coli, Klebsiella, Citrobacter and Enterobacter spp., E. faecium and E. faecalis). RMLIMS_LUCKNOW_2017.notes: Dr. RMLIMS Lucknow Microbiology News Letter, Issue 5 (March 2018), antibiograms for antibiotics and antifungals, January to December 2017. Each specimen table has one row per organism and location, the location shown only by the row colour: ICU, OPD, IPD (recorded as wards) and SRCLI (State Referral Centre for Laboratory Investigation, a separate location category, not recorded). Specimens: blood; body fluids (recorded as sterile body fluids); urine; respiratory specimens (sputum, BAL, mini BAL, throat swab and tracheal aspirate); pus. Organisms are printed at genus level in the blood and urine tables (Enterococcus, Citrobacter, Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Proteus, Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas spp.) and at species level in the other tables; "Pseudomonas spp." is recorded under the P. aeruginosa key. Rows are recorded as printed, including rows of 1 to 5 isolates (the report applies no minimum). The blood table has a single HLG/G column (high-level gentamicin for enterococci, gentamicin for staphylococci). Where the organism charts and the tables disagree on which location a row belongs to, the rows are not recorded (see excluded): the blood Enterococcus spp., CoNS and S. aureus OPD and IPD rows (the table colours give OPD n=15, 94, 15 and IPD n=5, 32, 8; the charts give OPD 5, 32, 8 and IPD 15, 94, 15, and the chart totals match each box), the body-fluid A. baumannii OPD and IPD rows (table OPD 1, IPD 8; chart OPD 8, IPD 1) and the pus E. coli OPD row (the row coloured OPD has n=55 and the one coloured SRCLI n=137; the chart gives OPD 137, SRCLI 55). Other chart and table disagreements are noted on the rows (blood IPD Enterobacter 14 against 40; respiratory ICU P. mirabilis 11 against 10 and no P. aeruginosa bar against 85 in the table; pus OPD E. faecalis 12 against 9). Counts are the ICU, IPD and OPD chart labels, including Candida spp. in blood and urine. The antifungal table prints numbers of isolates, not percentages, and is not recorded. The live URL returns 404; the PDF was downloaded from the Internet Archive copy of the same URL.

SGRH_2024.notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1), two years combined (January 2023 to December 2024), 8 pages. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococcus spp." (pus: "Staphylococci spp.") are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem/Meropenem" (blood and body fluid GNB tables) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure; the 2011 edition heads the same column "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin"); each such cell says so in its note. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Blood S. pneumoniae: penicillin and ceftriaxone hold the non-meningitis breakpoint columns; the meningitis-breakpoint values are in the cell notes. Urine and pus imipenem is printed "*Imipenem" with a footnote advising an alternative method before reporting Vitek 2 imipenem results for Proteus, Morganella and Providencia (noted on the Proteus cells). Colistin is not reported: the newsletter states that CLSI has had no susceptible category for colistin in Gram-negative bacteria since 2020. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts but their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Isolate numbers: the charts and the tables disagree by one isolate for 10 organism strata (blood ICU E. coli; urine ward E. coli and E. faecalis; urine ICU E. coli and P. aeruginosa; pus OPD K. pneumoniae; pus ward and body fluid OPD coagulase-negative staphylococci; body fluid ward E. coli and K. pneumoniae); each is recorded as printed and noted on its row. The body fluid ICU "others" list sums to 49 against "Others-50". Some percentages are not what rounding gives for the row's n (urine ICU Proteus n=12 prints cefuroxime 41 where 5/12 is 41.7, which suggests truncation), and a few match no count of the row's isolates at all (body fluid OPD Enterobacter n=13, cefepime 66; respiratory ward S. pneumoniae n=21, penicillin and ceftriaxone 97): per-drug tested numbers are not printed; all are recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Elizebethkingia meninseptica", "Sphinmonas paucimobilis", "Neisseria norrhoeae", "L.monocytogenes"); "Salmonella entertidis" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Serratia odorifera" as Serratia spp.; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 and 8 (case report, publications, highlights) and page 7 (antimicrobial consumption) are not susceptibility tables.
SGRH_2024.reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus/tissue, body fluids, respiratory specimens), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
SGRH_2024.method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2023 and 2024 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses); two years of data combined (Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1)) to improve denominators.
SGRH_2024.checking: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. Organism charts: legend and "others" entries were parsed from the text layer, checked arithmetically per panel (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, "others" entries sum to Others, legend counts equal the bar data labels) and compared by eye with the rendered charts. Two legend entries with a garbled number were read from the image and the bar label (blood ICU "E. coli1-53", bar 153; urine OPD "E. coli1-370", bar 1370), and one "others" entry the parser missed (pus OPD "Providencia spp.1-") was added from the image.

SGRH_2019.notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 26, No. 1 (published June 2020), data January to December 2019, 8 pages. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "June-2020"; the file downloads as mb-june2020.pdf). Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates with the repeat isolates excluded in parentheses, a data label on every bar and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Enterococci are reported at genus level only (printed "Enterococci spp.", urine "Enterococcus spp.") and recorded as Enterococcus spp. Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem / Meropenem" (urine, pus and body fluid GNB tables) under meropenem and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure), each cell noted; the blood and respiratory GNB tables print "Imipenem" alone (recorded under imipenem) and the body fluid GPC table heads its methicillin column "Cefoxitin" (recorded under cefoxitin). The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Colistin is printed as percent susceptible in every GNB table and is recorded as printed; urine Proteus prints colistin 0 in OPD and ward. Footnotes: blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin is printed "83*" with "*1 isolate IS, 1 isolate R", and respiratory S. pneumoniae OPD ceftriaxone "94*" with "*1 isolate IS"; both are in the cell notes. The body fluid GPC table prints Staphylococci spp. ICU as n = 0 with blank cells. Source inconsistency recorded as printed: body fluid OPD Staphylococci spp. (n = 9) prints penicillin 33 while its Cefoxitin column prints 0 (the build suppresses the penicillin figure). Isolate numbers: every table n equals the chart count of the same organism, specimen and location, and every chart panel balances (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the "others" list sums to Others). Per-drug tested numbers are not printed: 54 of the 820 recorded percentages are not k/n of the row's n (14 of them fit truncation, e.g. blood ICU A. baumannii n = 59, amikacin 13 where 8/59 is 13.6); all but three can be given by a smaller number of tested isolates, and all are recorded as printed. Three can be given by no whole number of tested isolates up to the row's n, rounded or truncated (pus ICU Proteus ertapenem 79 with n = 12; body fluid ward Enterococci spp. high-dose gentamicin 9 and linezolid 76 with n = 10): each is within one point of an achievable figure (the tolerance the app applies to every source for rounding), so it is shown without a caution and the arithmetic is in its cell note. Organism counts: every bar and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "S. maltophila", "L.monocytogenes", "Elizebethkingia meningoseptica"); "Salmonella entertidis" and "Salmonella typhimurium" are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Burkholderia vietnamiensis" as Burkholderia spp.; blood ICU counts Stenotrophomonas maltophilia twice (bar 18 and "S. maltophila-1" in the others list), both recorded. Fungi are counted in the charts as "Fungal isolates" (not recordable); the species also named in the same panels' others lists (blood ICU Cryptococcus neoformans 2, body fluid OPD and ward Candida tropicalis 1 each) are a partial count and are listed in excluded; fungal susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 (case report: histoplasmosis), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and the drug resistance index) and page 8 (case report continued, publications, highlights) carry no susceptibility tables.

SGRH_2011.notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 18, No. 1 (published April 2012), data January to December 2011, 8 pages; the older edition of the layout used in 2024. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism pie charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and GPC and GNB percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus, sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)" is recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci. Combined columns: "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) is recorded under meropenem and "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin" under vancomycin, each cell noted; the "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid separately (recorded). The pus and body fluid GNB tables print cefoperazone-sulbactam before piperacillin-tazobactam; every table was mapped by its own headers. Blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin is printed "90*" with the footnote "1 isolate was moderately sensitive". Colistin and tigecycline are printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and non-fermenters; no interpretive criteria are stated for them beyond "CLSI 2010". Isolate numbers: pus coagulase-negative staphylococci OPD (chart 87, table 82) and ward (chart 45, table 44) disagree; both recorded as printed and noted on the rows. The respiratory ward chart prints "Others - 54", but its "others" list sums to 43, and the legend plus 43 equals the printed 352 isolates. Several percentages cannot be produced by the row's n (per-drug tested numbers are not printed; for example pus ICU coagulase-negative staphylococci n=8, penicillin 11); recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Morgnella", "Elizebethkingia", "S. maltophila", "Strept. viridans" as viridans group streptococci); "Salmonella typhimurium" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts; their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. The live URL no longer exists; the PDF was retrieved from the Wayback Machine copy https://web.archive.org/web/20120512183945id_/http://sgrh.com/newsletters/mb%20apr%202012.pdf and opens completely (8 pages, 428 KB, not truncated).
SGRH_2011.reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in pie-chart legends and an "others" list.
SGRH_2011.method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2010 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).
SGRH_2011.checking: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text, so the pages whose GNB columns are in a different order map correctly; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. Organism pie charts (no data labels): legend and "others" entries were parsed from the text layer, checked arithmetically per panel (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, "others" entries sum to Others; the one exception, respiratory ward, is a source inconsistency described in notes) and compared by eye with the rendered charts. Names split over two lines in the "others" lists were read from the image.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,217 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 304, spread over all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6, plus every other cell), all 120 row n values and all 269 organism counts were read from the page images (tables at scale 3 to 4 cut into halves with the row labels kept; pie legends and "others" lists at scale 5; the cells not kept and the count mismatches again at scale 8 to 10) before comparing with the extraction.

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 304, whole file 0 of 1,217 cells, 0 of 120 n, 0 of 269 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink fills of the colour key, and every row n equals its OPD, ward or ICU pie legend entry apart from the two pus CoNS rows below); organism and specimen correct on every row (Pus wound swab as pus, Body fluids as sterile); every printed value of a recorded column is in the file, and the 9 table rows not recorded are exactly the 9 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% error threshold.

Combined columns: all 73 Imipenem/Meropenem cells (under meropenem) and all 42 Vancomycin/Teicoplanin cells (under vancomycin) carry their cell note. This edition has no Cefoxitin/Oxacillin column: all five GPC tables are headed Oxacillin alone and cefoxitin appears nowhere in the PDF, so the 24 oxacillin cells rightly carry no combined-column note. High Dose Gentamicin (9 Enterococcus cells) is recorded as gentamicin_hl; the Quinolones column is excluded, as notes say.

The 28 cells not kept (27 intrinsic, 1 caution) are all printed as recorded, none is a transcription error: blood S. pneumoniae gentamicin 0, 100, 0 (OPD, ward, ICU); Acinetobacter aztreonam blood 43, 25, 7, urine 8, 9 (OPD, ward), pus 7, 3, 0, body fluids 50, 0, 0 and respiratory 8, 0, 2; urine Proteus colistin 0, 0, 0; pus Proteus tigecycline 0, 0 and colistin 0, 0 (OPD, ward); respiratory Klebsiella ampicillin 0, 0, 1; caution: pus ICU CoNS penicillin 11 with n = 8 (conflict text accurate).

Count mismatches confirmed as printed (source inconsistency, already noted on the rows): pus CoNS OPD 87 in the pie legend against n = 82 in the GPC table, and ward 45 against 44. Each pus panel adds up to its printed Isolates total (778, 660) with 87 and 45, so the charts are internally consistent and the table n differs. Also confirmed: respiratory ward "Others - 54" against an others list that sums to 43 (legend plus 43 = the printed 352 isolates).

For readers of the counts: S. maltophilia is printed twice in the body fluids ICU and respiratory ICU panels ("S. maltophila" 1 and 3 beside "Stenotrophomonas maltophilia" 2 and 42); both entries are recorded as printed and the build sums them (3 and 45).

The document states no data period; the year is taken from the institution's own title for it on the Microbiology notice list ('Antibiogram 2023'), and no end month is given. Per specimen it gives samples received from ICU, OPD and wards (urine 586/471/507; blood 1839/9/426; sputum 164/90/325; pus 59/127/165; body fluids 1355 by fluid type), an organism distribution chart by setting, and percent-susceptible bar charts that are hospital-wide. Organism counts are recorded from the labelled urine (p3) and body fluid (p19) distribution charts only; the blood, sputum and pus distribution charts have no labels, so the counts cover only part of the isolates. Several printed figures are implausible for the organism (for example ampicillin 35% for blood Citrobacter and 85.7% for blood Klebsiella with Enterobacter); they are recorded as printed where kept, and the build marks intrinsic-resistance pairs.
