EASTPOINT.notes: A prospective study (Cureus 2024) at East Point Hospital and Research Center, Bengaluru, January to June 2022: 357 isolates from 345 inpatient samples (urine, blood, sputum, swabs and pus). Figures are % susceptible as printed; the study followed CLSI. It covers E. coli (131), Klebsiella (62, shown as K. pneumoniae), S. aureus (51), P. aeruginosa (36), Enterococcus (26, not speciated), P. mirabilis (11), Citrobacter (8), Acinetobacter (3) and Salmonella Typhi (1); the last four have very few isolates. Several printed figures are implausible: E. coli aztreonam 100%, clindamycin and linezolid results for Gram-negative bacilli, and S. aureus at 100% for ampicillin, amoxiclav, cefazolin and cefotaxime despite 41% for cefoxitin (implying about 59% MRSA). S. aureus vancomycin was printed as 0% and is not shown. No MRSA or ESBL rates were reported.
EASTPOINT.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Figures come from Table 2 (Gram-positive) and Table 3 (Gram-negative), page 4, headed 'Antibiotic sensitivity percentage (%)' (WHONET, CLSI), as printed; not-tested results were left out. The implausible Gram-negative figures (E. coli clindamycin 100% and aztreonam 100%; P. aeruginosa clindamycin 100%, nitrofurantoin 100%, linezolid 50%; Klebsiella linezolid 100%) and S. aureus cotrimoxazole 6% were entered exactly as printed. Streptococcus sp. (n=10), coagulase-negative staphylococci (n=8), Proteus vulgaris (n=9) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (n=1) are in the tables but not included. Acinetobacter sp. is shown as A. baumannii.

GIMSR_2018.notes: Pilli et al. (JMSCR 2019) report urinary isolates from outpatients at GITAM Institute of Medical Sciences and Research, Visakhapatnam, in 2018, taken from Table 2 of the paper. It covers E. coli (48 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (82). Figures are % susceptible as printed. Ampicillin is not given for K. pneumoniae, which is intrinsically resistant. The figures were transcribed from the paper and have not been re-verified in 2026. The data are more than seven years old and resistance has shifted since, as ICMR national trends show; check them against the current laboratory antibiogram before using them to guide therapy.
GIMSR_2018.checking: typed into the app from the paper; not re-verified in 2026

JSS_KLEB.notes: Neelambike Sumana et al. (Front Microbiol 2025) report a retrospective study of Klebsiella pneumoniae from urine at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, a 1,800-bed hospital, tested by VITEK 2 with CLSI breakpoints. Of 920 isolates from 2014 to 2023, only the 83 from 2023 are shown. The paper's Tables 3 and 4 have the S and R headers swapped (the column labelled S holds % resistant), as its own text and carbapenem-resistant counts confirm, so figures are 100 minus the resistance figures in the text and intermediate counts as susceptible. Carbapenems are one class figure (61.5%; 38.55% resistant, 32 of 83) shown for ertapenem, imipenem and meropenem alike; the ciprofloxacin figure is the paper's fluoroquinolone row, and the cefuroxime figure is oral cefuroxime axetil. Carbapenem resistance peaked at 66.13% in 2021 and was 41.84% (385 of 920) over the decade.
JSS_KLEB.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Figures are 100 minus the 2023 resistance percentages given in the paper's narrative (pages 3 and 8), not read from the mislabelled table columns. The aminoglycoside class result (30.12% susceptible, 69.88% resistant) is not shown because no single agent is named. Per-year figures exist for 2014 to 2023 (for example 2014, n=27: carbapenem resistance 3.70%, ceftriaxone 7.41%). Other uropathogens (E. coli 9,211, P. aeruginosa 1,108, A. baumannii 192, S. aureus 161, enterococci, Proteus) are counted in the paper without susceptibility data.

excluded.why: class-level result, not one drug
oral cefuroxime axetil (100 minus 91.57% resistant) printed beside parenteral cefuroxime; both map to one drug key, so the parenteral figure is kept

Only urine and pus were processed through 2024 (blood and stool from the last quarter of 2024; no Salmonella, Shigella or Vibrio cholerae isolated). The report states 1118 isolates from 946 patients; its specimen table (Table 1) totals 1009 priority-pathogen isolates.

KARSNET_ALAPPUZHA_2024.method: Conventional disc diffusion; WHONET; CLSI 2024 guidelines; one result per patient per specimen type and pathogen (1118 isolates, 946 patients).

KARSNET_SHIGELLA_2026.notes: Outbreak report, not a cumulative antibiogram: a 3-page Kerala Health note on the 2026 Shigella outbreak in Kerala (226 laboratory-confirmed cases and 7 deaths reported by 22 June 2026, more than the 133 cases of all of 2025), giving KARS-Net resistance figures for the 44 Shigella isolates of January to May 2026 and for the three previous years. The 2026 figures are part-year, outbreak-period data from few isolates (ampicillin 29 tested, chloramphenicol fewer than 30); they come from the outbreak period and may differ from sporadic shigellosis. All figures are percent resistant. The note's treatment advice (ciprofloxacin no longer suitable empirically; carbapenem first for shock or multi-organ dysfunction, ceftriaxone for other inpatients, cefixime or azithromycin, or co-trimoxazole or doxycycline, for outpatients) is not recorded as data.
KARSNET_SHIGELLA_2026.reporting: Percent resistant of Shigella isolates to six antibiotics by year (2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 up to May) from KARS-Net data, with the number of isolates per year; a line chart with a data table (image). Antibiotic-year combinations with fewer than 30 isolates tested are named in a footnote.
KARSNET_SHIGELLA_2026.method: KARS-Net laboratory surveillance data; the note does not describe testing methods or breakpoints.
KARSNET_SHIGELLA_2026.checking: The chart and its data table are an embedded image with no text layer: values read from page images (the image extracted at its native 1014 x 824 px and the table zoomed), every 2026 value checked against the chart's line labels, and the 2023 to 2025 columns checked against the KARS-Net annual reports for those years (same values). The small-numbers footnote is in the text layer.

KARSNET_2025.notes: Kerala state antibiogram (KARS-Net Annual Report 2026, released September 2026), data from 1 January to 31 December 2025: 55 of 59 network laboratories in 14 districts (government and private medical colleges, government hospitals and laboratories, private hospitals). All figures are percent resistant (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimen PA (pus aspirate) is shown under deep infections (aspirates) and OSBF (other sterile body fluids) as sterile. The specimen tables pool all location types (set all); blood rows by location (OPD, IPD, ICU) come from the bar charts. The Salmonella table covers blood and stool isolates together (recorded as all specimens). The all-specimen S. aureus (cefoxitin) and Enterococcus (vancomycin) rows carry the MRSA and VRE yearly trends. Drugs printed "-" (fewer than 30 tested) are left out.
KARSNET_2025.reporting: Percent resistant by pathogen and specimen (blood, pus aspirate, other sterile body fluids, urine; stool for Salmonella and Shigella), all location types pooled, with number tested and number resistant; blood isolates also charted by location type (OPD, IPD, ICU) with printed data labels; MRSA and VRE yearly trend charts.
KARSNET_2025.method: WHONET collation and analysis; CLSI interpretive criteria; disc diffusion, broth microdilution and automated AST at the sites; colistin by broth microdilution or agar dilution per the NARS-Net SOP; first isolate per patient, specimen type and pathogen (73,437 isolates reported, 65,849 unique-patient isolates). Percentages not computed when fewer than 30 isolates were tested.
KARSNET_2025.checking: Tables 4 to 11 parsed from the PDF text layer (words assigned to columns by x position) and every value compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2; each printed percentage was also recomputed from its printed counts (four disagreements are recorded as conflicts). MRSA and VRE trend labels read from the rendered charts (one bar per year in legend order). Count Tables 2 and 3 checked against the images and their printed totals. Page numbers are 1-based PDF pages.

KONASEEMA_GNB.notes: Padmaja et al. (Bioinformation 2025) studied Gram-negative isolates from the ICUs (MICU, SICU and CCIU) of Konaseema Institute of Medical Sciences, Amalapuram, June 2023 to July 2024. The paper gives no exact percentages, only bands for urinary isolates: 80% or more, 60 to 80%, and under 60%. A figure of 70 marks the 60 to 80% band, not a measured value; under-60% results carry no number; P. aeruginosa meropenem 80 comes from the text. The only exact figure is Acinetobacter tobramycin, 96%. Isolate numbers (K. pneumoniae 277, E. coli 244, P. aeruginosa 148, A. baumannii 93, Proteus 13) count all ICU isolates, not urinary ones, and the paper names only genera, shown here as the main species. Carbapenem results are for meropenem, the only carbapenem tested. The paper contradicts itself on some urinary agents, for example nitrofurantoin for Klebsiella.

SRM_CARBA.notes: A 2025 Frontiers in Medicine study of 8,359 non-duplicate Gram-negative isolates at SRM Medical College Hospital, Kattankulathur, Chennai, July 2022 to July 2024, tested by VITEK 2; 2,007 (24%) were carbapenem-resistant. Every figure shown is for the carbapenem-resistant isolates alone (E. coli 433, K. pneumoniae 733, P. aeruginosa 290, A. baumannii 388), so the figures are far lower than a general antibiogram would show and must not be read as the hospital's overall susceptibility. The paper prints % resistant, so figures are 100 minus %R and intermediate counts as susceptible. Only the few drugs quoted with numbers in the text are available. Carbapenem resistance was 48% in A. baumannii, 38.6% in K. pneumoniae, 24.18% in P. aeruginosa and 12.1% in E. coli.

Counts: Tables 1 and 2 (by specimen, all locations) and Tables 3 and 4 (by location, all specimens) are two views of the same isolates, recorded as spec x all and all x setting, with each organism's Total from Table 1 or 2 as the all x all count; IPD is recorded as ward. The Emergency column and the Others specimen column have no key and are not recorded, nor are cells printed as "-", so the recorded location or specimen counts add up to less than each organism's total. Tables 7 and 8 (percent susceptible by specimen for all Gram-negative or all Gram-positive isolates pooled) are not organism-specific and were not extracted. Up and down arrows (a change of more than 5 points from the previous half-year) are not values and are ignored. 22 printed percentages cannot come from any whole number of the isolates printed as tested and are more than 1 point from the nearest possible value (or rest on a note that contradicts Table 6); they are kept as printed and marked as conflicts. 35 other printed percentages differ by up to 1 point from any whole number of the isolates printed as tested (the percentage and the tested count appear to use slightly different denominators); these are kept as printed. AIIMS_BHOPAL_2021.notes: Annual hospital-wide antibiogram of AIIMS Bhopal for 2021 (Department of Microbiology): for each organism the number of isolates (n), and per drug the number tested and the number (percent) susceptible. No specimen or location split, so rows are spec all, set all; there are no isolate count tables and no printed grand total. The printed percentage (a whole number) is recorded with the number tested; where the printed susceptible count and number tested give a percentage more than 1 point away (or more susceptible than tested), the cell is marked as a conflict. Colistin is recorded as printed: most organisms show 0 (0%) susceptible, which the rules flag (CLSI has no susceptible category for colistin); E. coli and C. freundii print 6 (60%) of 738 and of 18, marked as conflicts. The S. aureus row is not split by methicillin; cefoxitin is the printed OXSF (cefoxitin screen) column. AIIMS_BHOPAL_2019.notes: ICMR AMRSN regional-centre surveillance report and hospital antibiogram of AIIMS Bhopal (ICMR AMR project team, Department of Microbiology), 1st September 2018 to December 2019: 3887 culture-positive isolates as printed, ICMR antibiotic panel only (not every drug the laboratory tested). Rows are the location-wise tables of Section B (whole-number percent susceptible with susceptible/tested counts) for urine, blood and Other samples, each by OPD, ward (printed WD or Ward) and ICU. Organisms are the report's groups: Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, Morganella, Citrobacter, Acinetobacter, CoNS and Enterococcus rows are genus groups (row notes say which species they contain), Salmonella is typhoidal Salmonella (S. Typhi, S. Paratyphi A, Salmonella spp.), and the blood Klebsiella row is K. pneumoniae only. Other samples means all samples except blood and urine (per the report): superficial infections, lower respiratory tract, deep infections, sterile sites, CSF and other sample types (1018, 291, 129, 78, 16 and 307 isolates in Section A). It is recorded as other specimens (not blood or urine), with specimen_as_printed, and each row's note gives the specimen mix of its location: superficial infections are 430 of 541 OPD, 565 of 1011 ward and only 23 of 288 ICU positive samples in this group (the ICU group is mostly LRT and other sample types). Also recorded: the carbapenem-resistant (CR) and carbapenem-susceptible (CS) subset tables (Section B V) for Acinetobacter, P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae and E. coli from all specimens except faeces (spec all), whose colistin figures rest on 1 to 24 selected isolates (mostly marked as broth microdilution in selected MDR isolates). Cells printed -, NT or blank are left out; five cells printed 0% with 0/0 tested are left out (see excluded). Where a printed percentage is not what its printed susceptible/tested counts give, the printed value is kept and marked as a conflict (7 location-table cells, e.g. E. coli ward other-sample meropenem 83% with 117/212 = 55.2%, which its chart also shows as 83%; and K. pneumoniae CR levofloxacin 48/31). The urine Citrobacter and CoNS rows print n smaller than their tested counts (see row notes). Counts: the number of isolates per organism group and location printed in the antibiogram tables (including 0 and groups printed without susceptibility data), plus the organisms outside these groups from the location-wise isolation tables (Serratia, S. maltophilia, B. cepacia, Candida, S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes printed as Streptococcus pyrogens, Providencia stuartii, and blood ICU Citrobacter). The report states that most groups have fewer than 30 isolates, that ICMR shows results only for at least 20 isolates, and that the antibiogram was valid until March 2021. Page numbers are PDF pages; printed page numbers in Section B are 6 lower. Archived copy used (the live site could not be reached): https://web.archive.org/web/20240629094055id_/https://aiimsbhopal.edu.in/AIIMSFiles/officialDownload/ICMR_AMR_Report_Hospital_antibiogram_2019-2020.pdf.

AIIMS_BHOPAL_2016.notes: Antibiogram 2016 of the Department of Microbiology, AIIMS Bhopal (released February 2017): percent susceptible bar charts by site of infection, Gram group and patient location, with a narrative. Only the chart of Salmonella from outpatient bloodstream infections is organism-specific, so the file has one row (blood, OPD, 2015 and 2016 pooled, n not printed); every other chart pools all Gram-negative or all Gram-positive isolates of a site (several also without data labels) and is listed in excluded. There are no isolate count tables. Also hosted at https://archive.aiimsbhopal.edu.in/news/antibiogram.pdf (identical file, per the census). Archived copy used (the live site could not be reached): http://web.archive.org/web/20220329141224id_/https://www.aiimsbhopal.edu.in/AIIMSFiles/annexuredImage/antibiogram.pdf.
AIIMS_BHOPAL_2016.reporting: Percent susceptible bar charts by site of infection (bloodstream, respiratory, skin and soft tissue, urinary), Gram group and location (OPD, IPD, ICU), some with data labels; no isolate numbers printed. Only one chart is organism-specific (Salmonella from outpatient bloodstream infections, 2015 and 2016 pooled).
AIIMS_BHOPAL_2016.method: Clinical isolates recovered at AIIMS Bhopal Hospital in 2016; for organisms with fewer than 30 isolates in 2016, isolates of 2015 and 2016 pooled (stated as in accordance with CLSI). The antibiotic panel was not the same throughout the period (irregular supply), so isolates were not all tested against an identical panel, as stated.

BVDU_PUNE_2020.notes: Area-wise antibiogram section (pages 9 to 30) of the Bharati Hospital Pune antimicrobial policy version 7.0 (2021-2022), with data for 2020. The report has no hospital-wide table. Rows kept: the critical care unit Gram-negative (p10) and Gram-positive (p11) tables and the OPD Gram-negative (p29) and Gram-positive (p30) tables. The report notes under the OPD Gram-negative table that these isolates are from returning patients. Ward departments (Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Orthopaedics, Paediatrics) and the NICU have their own tables only, with no combined ward table, so they are listed in excluded; because no ward rows exist, a combination of the OPD and ICU rows is not a hospital-wide figure. The Gram-positive tables print "CoNS" rows next to separate Staphylococcus epidermidis rows; the CoNS rows are recorded as other coagulase-negative staphylococci (not S. epidermidis). n is the printed "No. of patient"; most rows have fewer than 30 isolates. No isolate counts are recorded: the pie charts give percent shares only. Printed cells that are implausible for the organism (for example E. cloacae amoxicillin-clavulanate and cefuroxime values, P. aeruginosa co-trimoxazole) are recorded as printed.
BVDU_PUNE_2020.reporting: Percent susceptible ("sensitivity", whole numbers and some one-decimal values) by organism and specimen within each area (critical care unit, ward departments, NICU, OPD), with the number of patients per organism row; pie charts of the top isolates by specimen with percent shares only. Colour bands mark usefulness; grey cells are not indicated or not tested. No hospital-wide table.
BVDU_PUNE_2020.method: Not stated in the report (no AST method, breakpoint standard or duplicate-isolate rule given).
BVDU_PUNE_2020.checking: ICU Gram-positive table (p11) parsed from the PDF text layer by character position and compared value by value, all cells and all n, with the rendered page. The ICU Gram-negative table (p10) and the OPD tables (pp29 to 30) are embedded pictures without a text layer: read from the embedded images cell by cell (grid lines detected, each row re-laid out under its column names, header names read from rotated header crops), with every blank or filled cell checked against a pixel occupancy map of the grid; second pass: every recorded value and n compared with the printed cell on the page rendered at scale 4 (overlay sheets with the recorded value under each cell). Specimen groups were read from the rendered pages.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 771 cells and all 52 row n re-read from the page images and written down before comparing with the file: the three picture tables (ICU Gram-negative p10, OPD Gram-negative p29, OPD Gram-positive p30) from the embedded images at native resolution zoomed 2x to 3x, the ICU Gram-positive table (p11) from the page rendered at scale 4.5. This covers the seeded sample of 281 cells, with the picture tables sampled at 40% (p10 122 of 306, p29 59 of 147, p30 48 of 121; p11 52 of 197). 0 errors, nothing corrected; organism, specimen group (blood, CSF, pus, respiratory, urine) and setting agree for every row. One-decimal values fit their row n (6.2 = 1/16, 9.1 = 1/11, 6.8 = 5/73, 9.6 = 7/73).

Second reader: the 53 cells the validator does not keep (3 cautions, 30 intrinsic, 19 hidden, 1 suppressed) are printed as recorded. The suppressed OPD urine S. aureus penicillin 33 is printed with oxacillin 20 (n 7) on p30, a source inconsistency (row note kept). The caution ICU pus E. cloacae colistin 0 (n 2) is printed 0 on p10, beside imipenem 0 and tigecycline 0 with ertapenem and meropenem 100. The two vancomycin cautions added by the current rules are printed that way on p30: OPD pus CoNS vancomycin 89 (teicoplanin also 89, n 9) and OPD urine S. epidermidis vancomycin 50 (teicoplanin also 50, n 2).

Second reader: the "CoNS" rows are confirmed as other coagulase-negative staphylococci: p11 prints CoNS rows (blood 10, CSF 2, pus 5) beside separate Staphylococcus epidermidis rows (blood 22, CSF 2, pus 1, urine 1), p30 likewise (CoNS pus 9, urine 4; S. epidermidis pus 6, urine 2), and the p9 and p28 pie charts list "Staphylococcus, coagulase negative" apart from S. epidermidis and S. haemolyticus. The p9 and p28 charts print percent shares only, so recording no counts is right. Grammar fixed in the two OPD CoNS row notes ("pie charts (p28) list").

IGGMC.notes: Mohod et al. (Cureus 2026) report a hospital-wide antibiogram of 4,603 culture-positive isolates from all specimens at Indira Gandhi Government Medical College, Nagpur, May 2024 to April 2025. It covers E. coli (1,321), K. pneumoniae (1,051), P. aeruginosa (785), Acinetobacter (479, shown as A. baumannii), S. aureus (664), E. faecalis (98), E. faecium (54) and Salmonella Typhi (11). The tables print % resistant, so figures are 100 minus %R and intermediate counts as susceptible. Colistin, tested by MIC, showed no resistance in any Gram-negative organism. Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin were tested on urinary isolates only, and the enterococcal gentamicin figure is high-level gentamicin. MRSA was 48.72%, inducible clindamycin resistance 21.97% and VRE 0.77%. Salmonella Typhi figures come from the paper's text, not a table, and rest on 11 isolates.
IGGMC.checking: carried over from the app's earlier antibiogram data: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Figures come from Tables 2 to 4 (pages 6 to 8), converted as 100 minus %R. Results marked IR (intrinsic resistance), NR (not recommended by CLSI), NT (not tested), MIC (MIC only) or U (urinary isolates only) were left out or marked. Salmonella Typhi resistance from the page 7 text: ampicillin 78%, cefotaxime 49%, azithromycin 64%, levofloxacin 64%, cotrimoxazole 46%.

SKNMC_PUNE_2024.notes: Antibiogram section (printed pages 6 to 17, PDF pages 14 to 25) of the SKNMC and GH Antibiotic Policy for Hospital, Version 2.1, dated 15 December 2024 (implementation 1 January 2025). Only organism-level lists are recorded: the 11 'Pseudomonas (n=...)' lines, one per box, and the Respiratory-ICU Gram-positive list, which that box attributes entirely to Staphylococcus aureus (prevalence 100% of the Gram-positive cocci). The pooled Gram-positive and Gram-negative lists mix several organisms and are left out (see excluded), so this file does not give E. coli, Klebsiella, Acinetobacter or enterococcal figures even though the boxes name them. Syndromes are recorded as specimens: BSI as blood, UTI as urine, respiratory as respiratory, SSTI as pus. IPD is recorded as wards because each syndrome has a separate ICU box. There is no BSI-OPD box. The data period is printed only as 2024 without months; since the policy is dated 15 December 2024 it cannot include all of December 2024. The Pseudomonas n printed on each line does not match the Pseudomonas share given in the prevalence column (a percentage of the Gram-negative group), so it may count only tested or only P. aeruginosa isolates; recorded as printed. Pseudomonas lines print 'Pipracillin', recorded as piperacillin. Page numbers are PDF pages (printed page number plus 8).
SKNMC_PUNE_2024.reporting: Syndrome by setting boxes (BSI: IPD and ICU; UTI, respiratory and SSTI: OPD, IPD and ICU). Each box prints the total isolates, the prevalence (% of the group) of the most common pathogens, one percent-susceptible list pooled over all Gram-positive cocci and one pooled over all Gram-negative bacteria (each with the group n), and a separate percent-susceptible list for Pseudomonas with its n. No per-drug tested numbers; AST method and breakpoint standard not stated.
SKNMC_PUNE_2024.checking: Values parsed from the PDF text layer (positional parse of the sensitivity column, bounded per box) and compared value by value with the rendered pages (PDF pages 14 to 25, scale 2.2); parse and images agree for all 101 recorded cells and all 12 row n values.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 101 cells and all 12 row n values re-read against the page images (PDF pages 15 to 25, scale 2.2 to 3), each value read before comparing; 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

The 3 caution cells (Respiratory-OPD Pseudomonas, n=9: ciprofloxacin 45.5%, piperacillin-tazobactam 81.8%, ceftazidime 70%) and the 6 intrinsic cells (Pseudomonas cotrimoxazole, cefotaxime, doxycycline and amoxicillin-clavulanate 0%) are printed as recorded.

Confirmed on p21: the Respiratory-ICU box lists 'Gram Positive Cocci (n=23)' with one pathogen only, 'Staphylococcus aureus ss. aureus', prevalence 100, so recording that list as S. aureus is supported; the same box's Pseudomonas line (n=31) continues on p22.

Lead 2026-09-26 (review round 2): the 11 Pseudomonas rows are marked unreliable (values unchanged, as printed): the per-drug percentages cannot come from the printed isolate numbers (45.5% for a row of 9) and swing between 0 and 100 across boxes of the same organism (gentamicin 100% in urine wards, 0% in urine OPD; imipenem 0% beside meropenem 54 to 73% in urine), so each figure rests on an unstated number of tested isolates. They are shown with a caution and never pooled or used by the console or reasoning.
